m2c/src/m2c/__init__.py -- Patch C01: the M2C client package.

``m2c`` is the local half of M2C (Minime to Code): a Python command-line
client that will, in later work packages, store sessions on this machine
(C02), sign in with a device code (C03), keep a link to the MiniMe server
(C04) and execute tools locally (C05+).  This first patch (C01) is only the
skeleton: the package layout, the ``m2c`` console entry point, the config
directory, a content-free logging setup and a minimal ``m2c doctor``.

Design rules that every later patch inherits (build plan §0.2 and §1):

* Python >= 3.11 (decision D1) and the standard library only at runtime
  until a work package explicitly adds a dependency.  tests/test_cli.py
  enforces this.
* Security checks fail closed; telemetry and logging fail open.
* Nothing the user typed, the model produced or a tool returned is ever
  written to a log (see logging_setup.py).
* Everything the client keeps on disk lives under one directory, ``~/.m2c``
  by default, relocatable with the ``M2C_HOME`` environment variable so that
  tests never touch the real home directory.

This module deliberately imports nothing, so ``import m2c`` is free and the
version can be read by the build backend without importing the package.

Place this file at: m2c/src/m2c/__init__.py

m2c/src/m2c/checkpoints.py -- Patch C08: checkpoints and rewind.

Before an edit, ``snapshot()`` saves what the affected files looked like.
``rewind()`` puts the project back to the state just before a given step ran.
A bug here destroys the user's files, so this module is written around its
failure paths; the happy path is the short part.

What is stored, and where
-------------------------
* **Blobs**: ``~/.m2c/checkpoints/<session>/<sha256>`` (through ``paths``, so
  ``$M2C_HOME`` is honoured).  One file per distinct content, named by the
  SHA-256 of its bytes, so identical content is stored once per session
  (deduplication).  Directories are 0700, blobs 0600, whatever the umask.
  Every blob is written to a temp file in the same directory, flushed,
  ``fsync``ed and renamed into place, so a blob is either whole or absent.
* **The index**: one row per file per step in the C02 store's ``checkpoints``
  table, ``(session_id, step, path, blob_hash, ts, mode)``.  ``path`` is
  relative to the project root and uses ``/``.  ``blob_hash`` is NULL when the
  file **did not exist** before the step (so a rewind deletes it); ``mode`` is
  the permission bits, NULL exactly then.  ``mode`` is the one column this
  patch adds (migration v2 in store/migrations.py).  There is no index outside
  the store.

m2c/src/m2c/config.py -- Patch C01: settings that come from the environment.

Deliberately thin.  The client has three knobs so far, all environment
variables so nothing about them is written to disk:

    M2C_HOME        relocates the config directory (documented in paths.py)
    M2C_LOG_LEVEL   DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR | CRITICAL (default WARNING)
    M2C_SERVER_URL  where the MiniMe backend lives (added by Patch C03; C01
                    had no server setting).  There is no default: the public
                    address is not decided yet, so ``m2c login`` asks for it.
                    After a login the address is stored with the credential,
                    so later commands do not need the variable.

Later work packages (the store in C02, login in C03, the device link in
C04) read their settings through ``Config`` rather than reaching into
``os.environ`` themselves, so tests can pass a plain dict.

Failure policy follows the repo-wide rule: a bad *log level* falls back to
the default (logging fails open and must never stop the CLI), while a bad
*M2C_HOME* raises ``paths.ConfigDirError`` (it decides where credentials
are stored, so it fails closed).  A bad *M2C_SERVER_URL* fails closed too
(``ServerUrlError``): it decides where the device credential is sent.

M2C_SERVER_URL rules, enforced by ``normalize_server_url``:

* ``https`` only.  Cleartext ``http`` is accepted for loopback hosts

m2c/src/m2c/headless.py -- Patch C10: headless mode, ``m2c -p "task"``.

WHAT THIS IS.  One task, no terminal interaction: ``m2c -p "fix the failing test"`` signs in with the saved
credential, connects the device link (C04), starts a run (profile "code", the chosen mode, ``cwd_label`` = the folder's
NAME, never a path), sends the task as the user message and streams the reply.  It never prompts, it works without a
TTY (CI, cron, a pipe, another program such as Menux), and the task may come from stdin: ``m2c -p -``.  It is the
non-interactive sibling of the prompt loop in repl.py (I01); cli.py only parses the options and calls
``run_headless``.

    m2c -p "task" [--output-format text|json] [--mode plan|ask|accept-edits]
                  [--allow RULE]... [--deny RULE]... [--sandbox auto|required|off] [--cwd PATH]
    echo "task" | m2c -p -

                  by a line break.

m2c/src/m2c/logging_setup.py -- Patch C01: logging that can never record
message content.

The rule (build plan §11.4, applied to the client): nothing the user typed,
nothing the model produced and nothing a tool returned may appear in a log
line -- not in the message, not in a %-style argument, not in an ``extra=``
field, not inside a traceback.  Logs are what people paste into bug reports,
so "we only meant to log the id" is not good enough; the logging setup
itself has to make the leak impossible rather than rely on every future
call site being careful.

How, in layers (all enforced by tests/test_logging_setup.py):

1. ``log_event(logger, level, "dotted.event_name", key=value, ...)`` is the
   sanctioned way to log anything with data in it.  Only keys in
   ``SAFE_KEYS`` are emitted -- ids, counts, codes, durations: the same
   things §11.4 says the server may log.  Values must be numbers, booleans
   or short identifier-like strings; anything else becomes ``<redacted>``.
   A key outside the allowlist is not printed at all, only counted
   (``_dropped=N``).  Adding a key to ``SAFE_KEYS`` is a reviewed decision:
   never add one that can carry user text.

2. ``ContentFreeFilter`` is attached to the handler, so it also covers
   records produced by plain ``logger.info(...)`` calls:
   * %-style / mapping arguments are discarded -- the literal template is
     logged, the values never are (``log.info("user said %s", text)``
     prints ``user said %s``);
   * every non-stand

m2c/src/m2c/paths.py -- Patch C01: where M2C keeps its files on this device.

Per build plan §O1 the device is the source of truth, so everything the
client stores (the SQLite state database from C02, the device credential
from C03, logs, checkpoints, memory ...) goes under one directory:

    ~/.m2c/                     the default
    $M2C_HOME                   overrides it, when set and non-empty

``M2C_HOME`` exists so that tests (and anyone running two profiles side by
side) never touch the real home directory.  Rules for the variable:

* It must be an absolute path (``~`` is expanded first).  A relative path is
  rejected rather than silently resolved against whatever the current
  directory happens to be, because that would scatter credentials around.
* Set but empty counts as unset, the usual shell convention.
* It names the directory itself, not its parent: ``M2C_HOME=/tmp/x`` means
  files land in ``/tmp/x/state.db``, not ``/tmp/x/.m2c/state.db``.
* Parent directories that do not exist are created with default
  permissions; only the final directory is forced to mode 0700.

The directory will hold a device credential, so this module is a *security*
check and fails closed (build plan §0.2).  ``ensure_config_dir`` raises
``ConfigDirError`` instead of carrying on when the directory

* exists but is not a directory,
* is owned by a different user (for example ``sudo m2c`` with a user's HOME),
* or cannot be put into mode 0700 -- typically because the filesystem
  ignor

m2c/repl.py -- the walking skeleton's prompt loop (patch I01, "hello run").

WHAT THIS IS. The smallest terminal front end that joins C02 (local store), C03 (login) and
C04 (device link) to the server's text-only turn runner: after login, ``m2c`` shows a prompt;
each line you type is one message; the reply is printed as it streams. The real terminal UI is
C09 and replaces this module; nothing here adds a dependency (plain ``input()``, ``print``,
asyncio and threading from the standard library).

THE FLOW
  * The first message of a conversation starts a run: ``DeviceLink.start_run`` (profile
    "code", mode "ask", ``cwd_label`` = the folder's NAME, never a path). C04 creates the
    session in the local store in the same call. Every later message is
    ``DeviceLink.send_user_message``. Before it goes out, the message is appended to the local
    log as the client event ``user.message`` (the device log is the record; C04 skips non-server
    events when it recovers its resume cursor).
  * ``LinkCallbacks.on_event`` prints each ``text_delta`` as it arrives. C04 has already
    appended every server event to the local store before the callback runs.
  * A ``notice`` with code ``reply_restarted`` means the connection dropped in the middle of a
    reply and the server is writing it again from the start: the partial reply is discarded
    (it stays in the log, but it is not shown again, not counted and not stored as the reply)
    and one short line says so. A terminal cannot un-

m2c/src/m2c/runner.py -- Patch C24: the device tool runner, the glue between a proposed tool call and its execution.

SECURITY-CRITICAL: THIS MODULE DECIDES WHAT RUNS ON THE PERSON'S MACHINE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The server proposes a call (``tool_proposed``).  Nothing the server says is an instruction: this module asks the policy
engine (C06), asks the person when the engine says ask, takes a checkpoint (C08) before a file is changed, runs the
tool (C05 files and search, C07 shell) and answers with ``approval`` and ``tool_result`` exactly as protocol/README.md
sections 2, 3 and 5 describe.  Everything fails closed: a policy that cannot be read, an ``ask`` that returns garbage
or raises, a decision that cannot be recorded locally, a checkpoint that cannot be saved -- each ends in "not run".

m2c/src/m2c/session_setup.py -- Patch C10b: what a session needs to use tools, built once for the TUI AND for ``m2c -p``.

Before this patch the TUI built these pieces inline in ``tui/session.py``: the C05 ``ToolContext`` for the project folder
(checked by C05's path guard), the C05 shell configuration, the C06 rule layers, the C12 run context, and the C06 policy
context.  Headless mode needs exactly the same pieces, and the same policy: two copies would drift, and a difference
between them is a hole in a security check.  So the construction lives here, and BOTH callers use it:

    ``open_project``            the folder check, the ToolContext + ShellConfig, the layers and the run context
    ``project_policy_context``  the C06 ``Context`` for a mode (what ``TuiSession.policy_context`` returns)

What only headless mode uses (the TUI never calls these):

    ``parse_cli_rules``         ``--allow`` / ``--deny`` text -> C06 rules, validated with C06's parser
    ``with_session_rules``      those rules as a session-only addition to the user layer
    ``denial_hint``             the fixed words that say WHICH rule a refused call needed
    ``headless_tool_setup``     the ``tool_setup`` argument of ``headless.run_headless``: validates, then (``open``) builds
                                the C24 ``ToolRunner`` and wraps it in a ``ToolHost``
